subject: Urban Planning
title: The Aral Sea Disaster
description: A quick, practical guide to The Aral Sea Disaster.

hook.text: The Aral Sea was the fourth-largest lake in the world. Soviet planners drained it. Now it's mostly desert.

buildup.text: In the 1960s, rivers feeding the Aral were diverted to irrigate cotton fields. The lake began shrinking immediately.

discovery.text: By 2014, the eastern basin was completely dry. Fishing towns sit 60 miles from the nearest water.

twist.text: Toxic dust from the exposed seabed causes cancer and respiratory disease in surrounding communities.

climax.text: Kazakhstan built a dam and partially restored the North Aral. Fish are returning. But the south is gone forever.

punchline.text: They drained a sea for cotton. The cotton isn't worth the water.

quiz.question: Why did the Aral Sea shrink?
options: Climate change caused extreme drought in Central Asia
Rivers feeding it were diverted for cotton irrigation
An earthquake redirected underground water channels
